summary: Final-chunk stalls cause 120s request timeouts for very large max_tokens with function_call enabled
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DocuGrow is seeing consistent request-level 120s timeouts when they submit generation requests that combine: very large max_tokens (>=100k), long prompt prefixes (~50k tokens), and function_call: "auto" with structured streaming enabled. The request appears to run and stream chunks for the majority of the budget but stalls on the finalization step; after server-side stall the client sees a hard 120s keepalive timeout and the request ends with a 504. This affects multiple model variants and only appears in prod us-east.

Impact:
- Several production customers at DocuGrow hit intermittent failures for long exports and summarization jobs; observed error rate ~12% for token budgets >100k.
- SLO breaches for specific routes (export/long-summarize).
- Billing and retries caused duplicate downstream jobs.

Environment:
- prod, us-east
- Customer library: redwood-js v2.6.1 (streaming via SSE)
- Request flags: max_tokens=120000, function_call="auto", stream=true, prefer_fast_finalization=false
- Models: redwood-7b-v1 and fallback gptx-13b-quant

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) POST generation with a 50k-token prompt + max_tokens=120k + function_call:auto + stream=true
2) Receive streaming chunks steadily for ~90–110 seconds
3) Final chunk transmission stalls; server appears to hold socket until 120s and then returns 504 to client

Logs / Observations (from support capture):
- Application logs show streaming at ~60–75 tokens/sec then stall at finalizer stage.
- In serving runtime traces (sample): finalizer task shows a synchronous wait on "checkpoint-write" completing and a thread blocked in fsync for ~18s prior to the 120s cutoff.
- KV cache retention shows an on-demand checkpoint triggered when sequence length crosses 100k tokens for that model profile.
- No obvious 5xx surge in upstream infra; CPU on the worker GPU host spiked but not saturated.

Hypotheses / initial triage notes:
1) Finalizer is performing a synchronous KV-cache checkpoint when the request reaches a large sequence length, which occasionally stalls due to background I/O (fsync) and blocks the streaming final chunk.
2) Function_call structured output marshaling may add a large serialization step at finalization that increases blocking time.
3) When batching and backpressure coincide, the finalizer lock causes head-of-line blocking on the response stream.

Immediate mitigations provided to customer:
- Short-term workaround: lower max_tokens to <=40k or set prefer_fast_finalization=true to force non-blocking finalization path. Both reduce observed failure rate to <1%.
- Recommended client change: increase client-side streaming timeout to 180s for these long-run routes while we investigate.

Next steps / Action items:
- Eng (Linus) to reproduce in staging with a synthetic 120k-token request and capture finalizer traces (assigned).
- SRE to correlate worker host I/O patterns and check if checkpoint writes overlap with nightly maintenance jobs (cc: SRE infra team).
- Runtime team to evaluate making KV-cache checkpointing asynchronous for long-sequence requests or to move checkpointing off the critical finalizer path.
- Add a temporary rate-limit/batching guard to avoid combining large user token budgets with function_call=auto for enterprise routes until patch is released.

Notes on customer communication:
- Customer notified 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC; workaround accepted and applied. They asked to prioritize a permanent fix since exports are business-critical.
